subject: POC sprint charter + streaming API handshake
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: David Cho <david.cho@cardly.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC sprint charter + streaming API handshake

Hi David — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a proposed sprint charter so we can lock scope and owners for the POC.

Call recap (30 min):
- Goals: Validate Redwood streaming generation for Cardly’s automated dispute-response assistant; measure latency & cost at 99th percentile; verify function/tool-calling to your internal knowledge-base.
- Success signal (high-level): accept rate >= 85% on first-pass responses (per your evaluator prompts), median p99 latency < 350ms for common prompts, and a repeatable CI-driven evaluation harness.

Proposed 4-week POC sprint (high level):
Week 0 (this week): kickoff, data handoff (sample logs / anonymized disputes), account access, security checklist.
Week 1: integration sprint A — SDK + streaming route verification (developer leads), deploy local test harness.
Week 2: evaluation sprint — run automated scoring set (1000 prompts), collect latency/cost metrics, iterate prompts.
Week 3: stabilization & canary — A/B compare fallback to smaller model variant, run security review.

Ownership (proposed):
- Redwood integration lead: Dev Patel (dev@redwood.ai) — SDK wiring, streaming client, API routes.
- Redwood success metrics & eval: Laura Bennett (laura@redwood.ai) — evaluator script, pass/fail gates.
- Redwood commercial & POC sponsor: me (Marissa).
- Cardly tech lead: Sanjay Kumar (cc'd) — provide sample dataset & access to staging env.

Technical notes / integration checklist (short):
- Preferred path: Redwood streaming endpoint (/v1/generate_stream) using our streaming SDK (WebSocket or HTTP/2 chunked depending on your infra).
- Fallback: REST generate with chunked responses for environments that block WebSockets.
- Tool/function calling: we support JSON-defined tool schemas; we'll provide an example connector to query your knowledge-base API via a stateless adapter.
- Security: PII handling — recommend masking at source and test with anonymized records. For PCI-sensitive fields, we can route to Private deployment if needed (separate quote).

Attachments: POC_Charter_Redwood_v1.pdf (detailed milestones), streaming-api-spec.md (routes + example payloads).

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick alignment call Thu 04/12 10am PT to confirm scope & hit the security checklist items.
2) Cardly to share one-week sample (anonymized) by EOD Fri 04/13.
3) Redwood to provision trial creds and a short-run sandbox project by Mon 04/15.

If that aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite and the HubSpot POC record (HS-45871).

Thanks — looking forward.

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0173

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear rundown. High level yes — the objectives match what we discussed. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) Function calling: we absolutely need a deterministic way to map generated intents to an internal API call (we have strict auditing). Can the Redwood adapter surface the tool-uuid / schema and a signed execution trace we can record?
2) Data concerns: we cannot send raw card numbers. We will provide tokenized and masked dispute logs. If required, we can stand up a short-lived staging network for higher-sensitivity records.
3) Timeline: the team can deliver a masked one-week export by Friday EOD. We should aim to hold the Thu 10am PT alignment — Sanjay will join and is our eng lead for the POC.

Sanjay — tagging you for technical alignment on streaming (we prefer HTTP/2 over WebSockets if possible because of our proxy stack).

Appreciate you attaching the spec; I’ll review and flag any security gaps.

Best,
David
Director, Automation & AI | Cardly
david.cho@cardly.io | +1 202-555-0129

Hi David / Sanjay — quick technical notes to align on your two asks (function-calling determinism + HTTP/2 preference):

- Function-calling: our runtime will emit a structured tool_call object that includes tool_id, arguments, and a trace_id. We can add an HMAC-signed envelope (short-lived) so Cardly can verify the call origin server-side before executing. That envelope is persisted in logs and included in the event payload so your auditors can join traces.

- Streaming transport: HTTP/2 server-push + chunked responses is supported by our streaming SDK. If your proxy stack prefers HTTP/2, we will provide an example using gRPC-web or HTTP/2 chunked with TLS. WebSocket remains an alternative but not required.

- API routes: recommended for the POC
  - POST /v1/generate_stream (streaming chunks, includes trace_id header)
  - POST /v1/generate (non-streaming, full response)
  - POST /v1/tool_exec (for audit-only replay of tool calls)

- SDK: we’ll provide a Node + Python streaming client that wires into your existing worker process. The Node client supports backpressure and reconnection semantics; Python client supports asyncio chunk handling.

- Dev/ops note: for the trial we can issue expiring API keys scoped to the sandbox project; you do not need to provide production secrets. If Cardly needs an isolated tenant (for PCI) we can propose a Private deployment; that will require a separate procurement step.

Action items / owners (internal):
- Dev Patel: lead SDK + streaming wiring (deliverable: example repo + CI by Mon 04/15).
- Laura Bennett: provide evaluation harness and the initial 500 prompts for scoring by Tue 04/16.
- Marissa: finalize commercial terms / POC acceptance criteria.

David / Sanjay — can you confirm the staging URL pattern we should target and whether you prefer JWT or mTLS for the sandbox auth?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks for the quick replies and the technical alignment. Confirming the next steps and calendar invites: 

- Thu 04/12 10:00am PT alignment (sent invite) — agenda: review security checklist, confirm auth method, agree on sample export.
